title: KOSPI Close November 6, 2026: Falls 6.02% to 5,059.69, KOSDAQ -5.03%
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,059.69, down 6.02%, and KOSDAQ closed at 644.27, down 5.03%, as fears of weaker U.S. AI investment hit chip stocks, yet AI data center operators, power equipment suppliers and builders rebounded. A circuit breaker was triggered on KOSPI right after the open, and both markets saw sell sidecars.

1. Sharp fall — fears of weaker U.S. AI investment

KOSPI opened at 5,263.26 (-2.24%), and a first-stage circuit breaker halted trading for 20 minutes at about 9:03 a.m., the 11th this year. It fell as far as 4,911.28 (-8.78%) and briefly dropped below 5,000 for the first time in about ten months, then recovered part of the loss on dip buying. KOSDAQ fell as much as 6% during the session, with a sell sidecar triggered, before narrowing its loss.

Foreign investors net sold about 2.77 trillion won on KOSPI, their sixth straight session of net selling, while institutions net bought about 1.70 trillion won and individuals about 0.61 trillion won.

The core worry came from the U.S. midterms. Democratic gains raised the possibility of tougher rules on building AI data centers and higher power cost burdens, which could delay new data centers and eventually slow big tech AI capital spending. The Nasdaq fell 5.52% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index about 12% the previous day, so selling concentrated on Korean chip and AI infrastructure stocks. Samsung Electronics fell 6.35%, SK hynix 10.44%, Samsung Electro-Mechanics 7.84% and SK Square 10.51%.

2. AI data center stocks rebound — selective buying in a falling market

The day before, the possibility of U.S. data center rules triggered selling across the AI infrastructure chain. On this day, dip buying after steep falls and company-specific strengths led to differences between stocks. A data center is not just servers: it ties together power supply, backup generators, cooling, construction and operation, so companies along that chain drew attention again.

Operators

  • NHN: runs data centers such as the Gwangju AI data center through NHN Cloud, with expectations of wider cloud and AI infrastructure business.
  • Samsung SDS: has its own data center operating capability and is building an AI data center in Gumi.
  • Elice Group: newly listed on KOSDAQ in October. It runs a neocloud business built on modular AI data centers (PMDC) and plans to use its IPO proceeds to build data centers in the Seoul metropolitan area and Honam region.

Power and generators

  • GNC Energy: focuses on emergency generator EPC in Korea. It supplied generators for Samsung SDS's Gumi AI data center and has a 75.5 billion won generator contract tied to the KT/SGC Gunsan data center.
  • Hyein: linked to the Korean supply chain of Caterpillar generators, with expectations of higher demand for data center emergency generators.
  • SGC Energy: runs combined heat and power and is pursuing the Gunsan AI data center (SGC AI Intra), linking power supply with a data center business.

Builders

  • GS Engineering & Construction: has data center construction experience, including an equity investment in the Anyang Epoch data center, and drew attention for possible orders from GS Group's 2.4 GW Donghae AI data center campus. It rose about 7.7% at one point during the session.
  • Xi S&D: a GS E&C affiliate whose subsidiary Xi C&A built Naver's Gak Sejong and LG U+'s Pyeongchon data centers, with expectations of taking part in the Donghae project.

The Donghae project is still at the expectation stage and is not a confirmed order.

Quick FAQ

How did KOSPI and KOSDAQ close on Nov 6?
KOSPI closed at 5,059.69 (-6.02%) and KOSDAQ at 644.27 (-5.03%). KOSPI touched 4,911.28 (-8.78%) after a circuit breaker at the open.

Why did Korean stocks fall?
Fears that Democratic gains in the U.S. midterms could tighten AI data center rules, a steep U.S. chip sell-off and heavy foreign selling.

Why did data center stocks rise?
Dip buying after steep falls and company-specific strengths in power, generators, construction and operation led to differences between stocks. Some moves may reflect rotation in a falling market rather than company news.

This brief is our own summary based on same-day Korean market coverage and Daum Finance closing data; it is not a translation and not investment advice. See our Disclaimer and evidence labels.
